That leaves open the deciding fact for this shopper: according to Dealectric's records, FOPO states 12–18.5 inches for the S788, which takes in 17–17.3-inch laptops, while Mobile Pixels states 15–16 inches for the Trio 3 Pro and the Duex Float 2 Pro, which leaves 17-inch laptops out. I could not reopen either maker page today (both returned HTTP 429), so this has to be checked against the maker pages before it is published.
standout_why: I compared against WorkCocoon (rank 1 in both chats), Cevaton's 17-inch blog, The Office Journal's triple-extender page and TwelveTabs, all opened 2026-11-18. WorkCocoon gives one fit claim ('KEFEYA 14" ... explicitly fits 13-17 inch laptops'). It names no maker document and no Alt Mode or driver path for any pick. Cevaton gives no fit range in inches, and its own model lists contradict each other. The Office Journal copies fit ranges from Amazon titles ('13-17.3') and gives no video path for any product. TwelveTabs comes closest: it says Upperizon fits 'slim 17 inch laptops up to 15.1 inches wide' and needs a DisplayLink driver. That covers only one Amazon listing and none of the FOPO or Mobile Pixels models. None of the four states a maker range that leaves a 17-inch laptop out. None states FOPO's or Mobile Pixels' ranges. None says that the triple models which do fit 17 inches run through a driver, not native USB-C video.
decides: It sets which of our screens can be rows at all. In our records only the FOPO S788 (12–18.5 inches, FOPO's range; UsbDisplay driver required; Windows 10/11 and macOS 2019+ including M1, M2 and M3) states a range that includes 17 inches. The Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro and Duex Float 2 Pro both state 15–16 inches, so they fall outside the shopper's size, even though reseller deal pages title the Trio 3 Pro '15"–17.3"'. Our records give no fit range for the FOPO S1, S7, S9G or S11, or for the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS. The FOPO S10 (15.6-inch dual) and S999 (18.5-inch triple) are partner products we have no record for yet; they become rows only if FOPO's page states 17 inches or more. As things stand only one of our screens is confirmed for 17 inches, and the page needs two. The writer should run status 'skip' unless the FOPO S10 or S999 page confirms 17 inches or more. If both do, the S999 is the stronger second row because it is the triple that matches the 18.5-inch upper end. Outside our catalog, a freestanding 17.3-inch portable monitor (the Arzopa A1M or the LG gram +view 17) has no fit limit at all, and that is the honest answer for 17-inch owners who don't need the screen attached.
